title: Bengal STF Arrests Suspected Jaish Operative Linked to Pakistan Terror Network
excerpt: Mohammed Hamim Mondal was allegedly tracking the West Bengal Chief Minister's movements and planning to sabotage a student protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, according to investigators.
body:
• West Bengal STF arrested Mohammed Hamim Mondal, a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed operative, from Purba Bardhaman district for alleged links to Pakistan-based terror handlers
  • Investigators say Mondal was tracking Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's movements and had plans to sabotage a student protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar
  • Two associates — Arpita Sarkar and Aditya Singh — were subsequently arrested, with the probe uncovering an alleged honey-trap and surveillance network
  • The NIA has interrogated the suspects and may take over the investigation as the case expands

The West Bengal Police Special Task Force arrested a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed operative from a residential township in Burdwan, uncovering what investigators describe as a Pakistan-directed terror module that targeted the state's chief minister and planned disruptions at a major protest site in Delhi.

The Arrest and the Allegations

Mohammed Hamim Mondal, originally from Monteshwar in Purba Bardhaman, was arrested from Renaissance Housing in Burdwan and brought to Kolkata for interrogation. STF Inspector General Gaurav Sharma said at a press conference that the investigation had established Mondal's links with Pakistan-based handlers and that he was operating at their direction.

"The chief minister was one of the targets. Hamim had been assigned by Pakistan-based handlers the task of keeping a watch on the CM's movements. He was asked to gather information on the places the chief minister could remain unguarded."

— Gaurav Sharma, IG, West Bengal Special Task Force

Investigators recovered documents containing details related to Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's schedule, VIP movement plans, vehicle details, driver information, and parking arrangements. The STF said Mondal had also been instructed to buy police uniforms and head to Jantar Mantar in Delhi with a group to create disturbances at a student protest.

A Wider Network Unravels

Within days of Mondal's arrest, the STF apprehended two associates. Arpita Sarkar, described as Mondal's girlfriend and a social media influencer from Jharkhand, was arrested from Sahibganj. Investigators allege she played a key role in an alleged honey-trap network used to lure targets and gather sensitive personal information about political leaders in West Bengal.

The third arrest was Aditya Singh, a college student from Howrah, who investigators say came into contact with Mondal through an online gaming platform. The STF claims Mondal brainwashed Singh and assigned him to photograph the movements of a state minister's son, including the family's residence, vehicle, and daily routine. The photographs were allegedly shared through encrypted messaging applications.

Cross-Border Connections

The probe has revealed that Mondal was allegedly radicalized through social media before establishing contact with Pakistan-based operatives linked to the Shahzad Bhatti Network, a group the STF describes as involved in radicalization, narco-terror activities, and recruitment of youths for extremist operations.

Mondal was in contact with several handlers using aliases including 'Rana,' 'Uzair,' 'Abid Jatt 333,' and 'Hamad' through encrypted platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, Element X, and Session, after initially connecting on Instagram. The STF also recovered international SIM cards issued in the United Kingdom and Mexico from the accused, suspected to have been used for encrypted communication and for facilitating sleeper cell networks across India.

"Hamim was working under instructions received through social media and encrypted messaging apps from individuals using Pakistani handles and phone numbers."

— Gaurav Sharma, IG, West Bengal Special Task Force

Honey-Trap Recruitment

Investigators learned during interrogation that Mondal targeted aspiring models and social media influencers for the honey-trap operation. His assignment to recruit attractive young women was given by the Shahzad Bhatti Network handlers based in Pakistan, according to STF sources. Mondal's role was limited to initial contact — once connected, the Pakistan-based handlers would communicate with the targets directly.

What Comes Next

The National Investigation Agency has already interrogated Mondal, Sarkar, and Singh, and is likely to take over the case given its cross-border dimensions. The STF has indicated that further arrests are possible as the investigation continues to map the full extent of the alleged terror network and identify other members of the module.
nri_angle: The case highlights growing concerns about cross-border terror networks operating within India, a security issue closely watched by the Indian diaspora.
author: Diaspora Desk
